title: Encapsulation
body:
Combining a number of items such as variables and function into a single package.

The second half of the idea is **information hiding**: bundling the data together with the operations on it, and then exposing only a deliberate interface while keeping the internals private. Callers depend on what the thing *does*, not on how it stores anything, so the implementation can change without breaking them.

In C++ this is a class with `private` data members and `public` member functions. The same principle shows up well outside object-oriented code — a module system is encapsulation at the file level, which is exactly why [[Node.js]] needed one: without it, every file's variables would share one global namespace and packages would silently interfere with each other.
